outline.h2: Who can legally perform a marriage in Australia?
outline.answers: Primary keyword; related search 'Who can perform a marriage in australia' (Sydney, Melbourne); 'who can marry you in australia' AU 20; Paperlust and My Celebrant Buddy snippets
outline.notes: Direct answer in the first 100 words, 'as at November 2026': three groups authorised under the Marriage Act 1961 (Commonwealth-registered civil celebrants, ministers of religion of recognised denominations, state and territory officers). [[VERIFY: categories and wording against AGD and the Act, Part IV]]. 4 one-sentence key takeaways.

outline.answers: 'authorised marriage celebrant' AU 50, 'civil celebrant' AU 260, 'religious celebrant' AU 20; Wedlockers snippet 'civil celebrants and ministers of religion'; NSW Registry result (#8 Sydney); Wikipedia (Melbourne)
outline.notes: Explain the difference, not how to choose (that belongs to /expert-advice/how-to-choose-a-wedding-celebrant). [[VERIFY: recognised denomination list and the 'religious marriage celebrant' subdivision on AGD]].

outline.h2: Can a friend or family member marry you?
outline.answers: 'can a friend marry us australia' (SERP titles #4 Sydney, #5 Melbourne; My Celebrant Buddy #9/#7); The Knot #1 'Can Anyone Officiate a Wedding?'
outline.notes: Australia has no one-day or online-ordination route, unlike New York (one-day officiant licence) and US online ordination, which dominate the US SERP and confuse AU searchers [[VERIFY: AGD position]]. Practical answer: friend leads the ceremony, authorised celebrant does the legal parts. Do not quote competitor copy.
